integrity: The foundational monograph's publisher record was checked for the 1 August 1983 hardcover date, and mathematical bibliographic records were checked for the ordinary-differential-equations classification including MSC 34C15. A complete open 2015 review was inspected through its Guckenheimer–Holmes section and across the full article text; targeted searches found no invariant-measure, moment, or covariance formulation, while unrelated uses of average were distinguished. A 2018 same-object coupled-cell review was compared for its heteroclinic-network coverage and accessible full article text. Published semantic searches covered direct and equivalent invariant-measure, conditional competitor-load, RMS, per-capita-growth, and generalized Lotka–Volterra formulations. The cutoff-logarithmic proof, circulant determinant, variance defects, and rational specialization were independently reconstructed and replayed with the packaged checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem applies to compact invariant measures giving zero mass to all coordinate planes; boundary heteroclinic measures are excluded.
Individual RMS locking requires the nondegeneracy that the three interaction coefficients are not all equal.
The theorem gives selected conditional moments and speed defects, not the full invariant distribution.
It does not establish existence of an interior periodic or chaotic invariant state.
Global zero-average per-capita growth balances have generalized Lotka–Volterra antecedents; the originality claim centers on the stronger fiberwise conditional laws and exact defects.
An equivalent conditional identity could remain in unindexed heteroclinic-cycle or population-dynamics literature.
title: Fiberwise competitor-load calibration and RMS locking in the Guckenheimer–Holmes cycle
